epigrafe.descrizione: Roman copper alloy coin, probably a nummus of Crispus as Caesar dating from AD 324 to 325 (Reece Period 16). Reverse type PROVIDENTIAE CAESS camp gate with two turrets, without doors, star above. Probably minted in Trier (mint-mark: -/-PTR?). Diameter 16mm, and the weight 1.99g. Obverse inscription [FL IVL CRIS]PVS NOB CAES. Reverse inscription PROVIDEN - [TIAE CAESS]

epigrafe.descrizione: Roman coin: A copper-alloy radiate, contemporary copy, of Carausius dating to the period AD 286 to 293 (Reece Period 14). The obverse legend DIVO CARAVS(SIO?) is notable. The reverse is unclear. There is no clear prototype for this coin. It is probably that the die-engraver was inspired by a DIVO CLAVDIO coin of Claudius II (died AD 270). This coin is included in Sam Moorhead's corpus for RIC

epigrafe.descrizione: Silver denarius of Vespasian (AD 66-79). Mint of Rome , AD 70. Obverse has a laureate head facing right with the legend IMP CAESAR [VESPASIANVS] AVG. The reverse has Pax seated facing left, holding branch and caduceus and the legend COS [ITER T]R POT (RIC II (2nd ed), p. 16, no. 10; Reece Period 4). Diameter: 17.56mm; weight: 2.4g. Similar WREX-C00D49

epigrafe.descrizione: A copper alloy bow brooch of the Wirral type dating to the Roman period. The object is a hinged example. The head is stepped as is typical of this type with yellow enamel decorating each step. The headloop missing due to ancient breaks. The upper bow is decorated with three raised vertical panels which have been damaged. These are typically infilled with alternating cells of coloured enamel. Only…
